clue.text: One simply celebrated, having reduced weight?

parts.note: reduced, as in lowered, means low
mass is a measure of weight

explanation.surface: Someone modestly feted, or perhaps a dieter who has slimmed down.
explanation.walkthrough: A Low Mass is a Roman Catholic Mass said without music or ceremony, hence 'simply celebrated'; priests celebrate Mass.
explanation.definitionFit: A said service without singing or incense is the plainest form of the Catholic Eucharist, celebrated simply.

clue.text: After treatment, Brian and Lucy's first baby born in autumn

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of the word Lucy's is taken
the name has undergone treatment, that is been processed, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Following medical treatment, Brian and Lucy's first child arrives in the autumn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After treatment' is the anagram signal, not a medical scene. A Libran is born under Libra, roughly 23 September to 23 October, which falls in the northern autumn.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone born under the sign of the Scales, in late September or October, has that star sign.

clue.text: A silly" place for flowers

parts.note: read silly as sill-y, sill-like: a container for flowers set on a window sill

explanation.surface: Somewhere absurd to grow flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation mark is a scan fault for the setter's play on 'sill-y': on a sill.
explanation.definitionFit: A long trough for plants fixed to an outer window ledge is where flowers grow on a sill.

clue.text: Lack opportunity for fonder relationship

definitions.meaning: a lack, meaning a want or missing of something
from the proverb that being apart makes the heart grow fonder

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition alludes to the saying 'absence makes the heart grow fonder'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being away is both a lack and, proverbially, what makes the heart grow fonder.

clue.text: Oscar, for example, achieved by, a small cast

definitions.meaning: an Oscar is a gold award figurine given by the film academy
a small sculpture cast in metal or plaster

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a film winning an Oscar with few actors; 'cast' is a casting, not actors.
explanation.definitionFit: An Oscar is a little figurine, and a little cast figure is the same thing.

clue.text: Break piece of crockery, catching shelf

indicators.note: the cup catches, that is takes in, the shelf word, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a cup is a piece of crockery
a rack is a shelf for storing things

explanation.surface: A bit of china gets smashed as it snags on a shelf.
explanation.definitionFit: To crack up is to break down, mentally or physically, as a verb.

clue.text: Sets of rules start to cramp poetry

indicators.note: start to means the opening letter of the next word is taken

parts.note: odes are poems, so poetry

explanation.surface: Strict formal rules begin to cramp a poet's verse.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal or professional set of regulations is a body of rules.

clue.text: Loan may become an irregular event

indicators.note: the words become something else, so their letters are rearranged into a new word

explanation.surface: Taking out a loan may turn into something unusual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'become' rearranges LOAN MAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Something departing from the norm is an oddity or deviation.

clue.text: Boat picture has not succeeded, for a start

indicators.note: has not means the picture word lacks the letter for succeeded
for a start places the removed letter at the front of the word

parts.note: a sketch is a quick picture
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, used in genealogies

explanation.surface: A painting of a boat has failed to get off the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has not' and 'for a start' remove S from the front of SKETCH. A ketch is a two-masted sailing boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-masted sailing vessel is a type of small ship.

clue.text: New diagram at bottom of page, for example

indicators.note: in a down entry, the rearranged diagram sits at the bottom, below the page letter
new means the letters are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A fresh diagram printed at the foot of a page, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges DIAGRAM to ARADIGM, which goes below P because this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A model or pattern to be copied is a standard example.

clue.text: Structured play area in park

parts.note: reads like a playground for children, but means a built structure in a park where musicians play

explanation.surface: An organised children's playground in a public park.
explanation.definitionFit: A raised, roofed platform in a park is where brass bands perform outdoors.

clue.text: Run from start to finish of course, being shot

indicators.note: the run letter leaves the front of the course word and goes to its end

parts.note: a route is a course taken
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Someone jogs the whole length of a course, perhaps while under fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from start to finish' looks like it describes running a course, but it shifts R from the front of ROUTE to the back. In archery or shooting, an outer is a shot hitting the outer ring of a target.
explanation.definitionFit: In target shooting, a hit landing in the ring outside the bull and inner is called by that name.

clue.text: A crop of fruit

parts.note: corn is a cereal crop

explanation.surface: A harvest of fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The nut of the oak tree is botanically its fruit.

clue.text: He's cut and otherwise not hurt

indicators.note: otherwise means in a different way, so these letters are put in a different order

parts.note: the fodder, taken letter by letter with He's as HES

explanation.surface: A man has been cut, yet in other respects he is unharmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'otherwise' rearranges HESCUTAND; the surface's cut man is, ironically, unharmed.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming through without a scratch means being left unharmed.

clue.text: Year's ban light, having fallen foul of this?

definitions.text: Year's ban light, having fallen foul of this?

indicators.note: letters that have fallen foul are tangled up, so these words are rearranged

parts.note: the S of Year's counts here as a letter of the fodder

explanation.surface: A motorist given a year's driving ban, having failed a roadside test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having fallen foul' rearranges YEARS BAN LIGHT. The whole clue also describes the scene: a year's ban, a light sentence perhaps, for failing a breath test.
explanation.definitionFit: Testing drivers' breath for alcohol is what leads, on failure, to a driving ban.

clue.text: Daughter holding up a ring one dropped

indicators.note: in a down entry, the daughter letter is at the bottom, holding up the rest

parts.note: a band is a ring, as a wedding band
taken as written

explanation.surface: A daughter delays one ring while it is held up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding up' puts D underneath A BAND ONE in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Something given up or deserted has been left behind.

clue.text: In one position, holding up King. David, for one

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the reversed king goes in, that is inside, the position word

parts.note: a site is a position or location

indicators.note: in a down entry a word held up is lifted, reading from bottom to top, so reversed

parts.note: Lear is Shakespeare's king

explanation.surface: A king being propped up in one position, as with David.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding up' reverses the king because this is a down entry, read upwards; the reversed name splits the position word after its first letter. King David ruled ancient Israel.
explanation.definitionFit: King David was a member of the ancient Hebrew people descended from Jacob.

clue.text: I am experienced as better

parts.note: I am contracts to I'm
proved means tested by experience, so experienced

explanation.surface: Someone claims their experience makes them superior.
explanation.definitionFit: Something made better has been enhanced or upgraded.

clue.text: Inconsistent figures given in speech

parts.note: reads like numbers that don't add up in an address, but means figures of speech that clash with each other

explanation.surface: A speaker quotes statistics that don't tally.
explanation.definitionFit: Combining incompatible images in one expression, like 'stepping up to the plate in a sea of troubles', is that figure-of-speech fault.

clue.text: Estate is run down, we're told

indicators.note: we're told signals that the word is heard spoken, not written

parts.note: to run down is to belittle, to demean

explanation.surface: Someone reports that a country property has fallen into disrepair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link. A demesne is land attached to a manor house, kept for the owner's use.
explanation.definitionFit: Manorial land kept by the lord for his own use is a landed property.

clue.text: One knows one's past caring for this subject

definitions.text: One knows one's past caring for this subject

parts.words: One knows one's past caring for this subject
parts.note: reads as someone no longer caring, but means a person who cares for the past chooses this school subject

explanation.surface: Someone realises they have stopped caring about a topic.
explanation.definitionFit: Study of past events is the school subject for anyone who cares about times gone by.

clue.text: Author of futuristic yearbook

parts.note: reads as an annual's writer, but means the writer of a novel set in the future whose title is a year

explanation.surface: A writer who compiles an annual set in the future.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'yearbook' is the novel Nineteen Eighty-Four.
explanation.definitionFit: The English novelist who wrote the dystopia titled with the year 1984 is that writer.

clue.text: Advise socialist to keep statement short

indicators.note: the socialist word keeps, that is holds, the shortened statement inside it

parts.note: red is a common term for a socialist

indicators.note: short means the final letter is cut off the statement word

parts.note: a comment is a statement

explanation.surface: A left-winger is advised to make their remarks brief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' drops the last letter of the statement word, and 'to keep' puts what remains inside the socialist word.
explanation.definitionFit: To advise someone is to counsel or suggest a course to them.

clue.text: Leave shortly before a line dance

indicators.note: shortly means the leave word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: congé is leave or permission to depart

explanation.surface: Someone departs just before a dance in a row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' trims CONGE to CONG. A conga is a dance in a long single-file line.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cuban dance performed by people in a single-file chain is danced in a line.

clue.text: Foreign resident no longer a soft touch

parts.note: ex means former, no longer
a pat is a soft touch with the hand

explanation.surface: A person living abroad is no longer easily taken advantage of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a soft touch' suggests a gullible person, but here it is a gentle tap.
explanation.definitionFit: An expatriate is someone living outside their native country.

clue.text: Provide guidance as prophet, over time

indicators.note: the prophet word goes over, that is covers, the time letter, putting it inside

parts.note: a seer is a prophet

explanation.surface: A prophet offering advice about the passage of time.
explanation.definitionFit: To guide a course or person is to direct them.

clue.text: Initially visible to East, heavenly body coming back into view

definitions.text: Initially visible to East, heavenly body coming back into view

indicators.note: initially means only the opening letter of the next word is taken
coming back means the heavenly body word is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: the sun is a heavenly body

explanation.surface: A planet appearing low in the eastern sky as it returns to view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming back' turns SUN to NUS. The whole clue also describes the planet, which reappears as the morning star in the east.
explanation.definitionFit: The second planet from the sun, seen as the morning star in the east before dawn, fits the whole description.

clue.text: Strongly criticise volume I'm immersed in for entertainment

parts.note: to pan is to criticise harshly, as a critic does

indicators.note: the I'm letters are immersed in, that is put inside, the volume word

parts.note: a tome is a large volume or book
taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A critic slates a book while engrossed in it for fun.
explanation.walkthrough: Pantomime is a British Christmas stage show for families, with slapstick, songs and audience participation.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional Christmas stage show is a popular form of theatre for families.

clue.text: Time church set about using local language

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the time, church and set words together are read backwards

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
laid means set, as a table is laid or set

explanation.surface: A church adopts the vernacular at the appointed time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns the whole run TCELAID backwards, giving DIAL + EC + T.
explanation.definitionFit: A regional variety of speech is a form of a tongue spoken in one area.

clue.text: Right-wing group of conspirators, a solid and powerful pack (3,4) 10

parts.note: in British politics a dry is a hard-line right-wing Conservative
a cell is a small group of plotters within a larger organisation

explanation.surface: A tough, determined band of right-wing plotters.
explanation.walkthrough: The trailing '(3,4) 10 (7)' is page debris from the scan. A DRY was a Thatcher-era right-wing Tory, opposed to the moderate 'wets'.
explanation.definitionFit: A battery whose electrolyte is a paste rather than a liquid is a compact power source.
